about: The [[wikilink]] and ![[embed]] targets in a note's text, in order, as written: without a #heading, ^block or |alias, trimmed. Empty targets are left out. Markdown [text](path) links are not in this file.
typescript: wikilinkTargets in src/shell/linksTags.ts (the Outgoing links view)
rust: parse_note in src-tauri/src/index/parse.rs: the targets of its links that are not markdown links

cases.name: ^ without #
cases.note: TS cuts the target at ^ as well as # and |. Rust cuts at | and # only, so it gives "C^abc". Unverified in Obsidian, which writes block links as [[C#^abc]].

cases.name: a [ inside the target
cases.note: TS allows [ in a target; Rust skips any [[...]] with a bracket inside. Unverified in Obsidian.

cases.name: escaped pipe in a table cell
cases.note: Inside a table, \| is how [[Note|alias]] is written. Rust reads it that way ("Note"); TS keeps the backslash ("Note\"). Obsidian resolves it to Note. TS is likely wrong here.

cases.name: unclosed fence runs to the end
the other marker closes a fence (TS)
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets toggles on any fence line, so ``` closes the ~~~ block and [[B]] ends up inside a new one. Rust (and CommonMark, so likely Obsidian) only closes on the same marker. tagsInText's fence rule also agrees with Rust (see tags.json).

cases.name: a shorter fence closes a longer one (TS)
cases.note: As above: TS's wikilinkTargets ignores fence length. Rust and CommonMark need a closing fence at least as long.

cases.name: fence indented with a tab
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets allows any spaces or tabs before a fence; Rust allows up to 3 whitespace characters, tabs included. Both open a fence here. In CommonMark a tab is 4 columns, so this is an indented code line and not a fence; tagsInText agrees with that (see tags.json).

cases.name: fence indented 4 spaces
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets opens a fence at any indent. Rust, tagsInText and CommonMark allow at most 3 spaces, so this is not a fence.

cases.name: closing fence indented 4 spaces
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets and Rust's fence_close both close at any indent. tagsInText and CommonMark need at most 3 spaces, so the block runs to the end.

cases.name: closing fence with text after it
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets closes on any line starting with ```. Rust, tagsInText and CommonMark do not close on a fence line with text after it.

cases.name: a backtick in a backtick fence's info string
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets opens a fence on any line starting with ```. Rust, tagsInText and CommonMark: a backtick in the info string means it is not a fence.

cases.name: inline code
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets does not skip inline code. CONTRACT.md says links in inline code are skipped, and Rust does that. TS is likely wrong here.

cases.name: double-backtick inline code
cases.note: Rust blanks CommonMark code spans (any run length). TS's wikilinkTargets does not skip inline code at all.
